data.name: Help_Camera_Q1_Answer1
data.value: Remove the sticker from the camera lens.

data.name: Help_Camera_Q1_Answer2
data.value: Ensure the camera USB cable is securely plugged in to the Nano.

data.name: Help_Camera_Q1_Answer3
data.value: If nothing else will work, use a spare camera to test connectivity.

data.name: Help_Camera_Q1_Answer4
data.value: Call CattleSorting support if it still won’t connect.

data.name: Help_Camera_Q2
data.value: Any tips when calibrating distance to floor?

data.name: Help_Camera_Q2_Answer1
data.value: The chute should be set to the width that it is for processing. This usually means not too wide but not too narrow.

data.name: Help_Camera_Q2_Answer2
data.value: Do not include the side/wall of the chute when selecting the four corners of the floor.

data.name: Help_Camera_Q3
data.value: What if I can’t calibrate distance to the floor?

data.name: Help_Camera_Q3_Answer1
data.value: Try measuring from camera lens to both high and low rungs on the floor mat.

data.name: Help_Camera_Q3_Answer2
data.value: Clean floor mat or remove debris if it has built up on the floor.

data.name: Help_Camera_Q3_Answer3
data.value: If you still can’t calibrate then, call CattleSorting support.

data.name: Help_Common_Desc_ContactUs
data.value: If you can not address the problem based on above instructions, please contact us at:

data.name: Help_LFEID_Q1_Answer1
data.value: Is the LF EID a wand (Bluetooth) or a direct RS232 connection? If direct RS232, then select "wand already connected to Firefly" and proceed to testing.

data.name: Help_LFEID_Q1_Answer2
data.value: Is the wand a "smart" wand meaning it can connect to Bluetooth from the wand itself? If so then use the wand to find and connect to the Firefly directly.

data.name: Help_LFEID_Q1_Answer3
data.value: Is the wand a "dumb" wand meaning it has no display? If so then use the installation module LF EID connection scan dialogue to scan and connect to the wand.

data.name: Help_LFEID_Q1_Answer4
data.value: Do you see more than one wand? Try to isolate the correct one first then turn off the other one(s).

data.name: Help_LFEID_Q1_Answer5
data.value: Test with a cell phone. Can your cell phone see both the wand and the CattleSorting system’s Bluetooth (should be named like FireFly_XXXX, where XXXX are some numbers)? If not, then troubleshoot the Bluetooth device that is not appearing.

data.name: Help_LFEID_Q2_Answer1
data.value: In some cases the Firefly cannot be put in Command Mode. The installer needs to be able to see the Firefly to check the green light on the Firefly if the system reports it cannot scan for Bluetooth devices or connect to a selected device. The Firefly has 3 modes: Standby, Connected, and Command Mode. If the Firefly is in Standby the lights will flash once every 2 seconds. If the Firefly is Connected to a Bluetooth device, the light will remain solidly on. If the Firefly is in Command Mode, the lights flash quickly, several times a second. Sometimes the Firefly becomes stuck in Command Mode and the installer will need to physically reboot the Firefly if it continues flashing rapidly more than 2 minutes after last trying to configure the Firefly. If the Firefly still doesn't respond and remains in fast flashing mode, or immediately connects and will not enter Command Mode, flip it over and turn on DIP switch #1 before rebooting the Firefly and then toggle this DIP switch 2x to factory reset it, at which point you will see a brief flash on the light. For a Firefly that needs to connect to a wand (wand does not have the option to select a target), DIP switch #3 should be ON, all others OFF. For a Firefly that is selected by a wand, all DIP switches should be OFF.

data.name: Help_Network_Q1_Answer1
data.value: Check the Ethernet cable and connection.

data.name: Help_Network_Q1_Answer1_1
data.value: Make sure the Ethernet cable is securely plugged into the Ethernet port on both your router and Nano. On your router, make sure the Ethernet cable is plugged into the correct Ethernet port – not the internet port that’s used to connect your modem and router.

data.name: Help_Network_Q1_Answer1_2
data.value: If using Ethernet and the system dialogue reports the Ethernet is unplugged, check the cables between your facility’s equipment and the CattleSorting system. A cable tester or a separate cable is often the easiest way to test cabling. Your facility’s equipment should show a solid light on the Ethernet jack that is connected to the CattleSorting system, if this shows a solid light but the system dialogue still says Ethernet is not connected, contact CattleSorting support. It may also show a blinking light – solid light means connected, blinking means data is being sent successfully.

data.name: Help_Network_Q2_Answer1_1
data.value: If the WiFi network is showing up and works ok on your cell phone but still won’t connect to the CattleSorting system, then call CattleSorting support.

data.name: Help_Network_Q2_Answer1_2
data.value: If the WiFi network is not working on your cell phone, then contact the feedyard for troubleshooting or follow the steps below.

data.name: Help_Network_Q2_Answer2
data.value: Restart your modem and wireless router.

data.name: Help_Network_Q2_Answer2_1
data.value: This helps create a new connection to your internet service provider (ISP). When you do this, everyone that is connected to your Wi-Fi network will be temporarily disconnected. The steps you take to restart your modem and router can vary, but here are the general steps.

data.name: Help_Network_Q2_Answer2_1_1
data.value: Unplug the power cable for the router from the power source.

data.name: Help_Network_Q2_Answer2_1_2
data.value: Some modems have a backup battery. If you unplug the modem and the lights stay on, remove the battery from the modem.

data.name: Help_Network_Q2_Answer2_1_3
data.value: Wait at least 30 seconds or so. If you had to remove the battery from the modem, put it back in.

data.name: Help_Network_Q2_Answer2_1_4
data.value: Plug the modem back into the power source. The lights on the modem will blink. Wait for them to stop blinking.

data.name: Help_Network_Q2_Answer2_1_5
data.value: Plug your router back into the power source.

data.name: Help_Network_Q3_Answer1_Desc2
data.value: CattleSorting can still function with a poor internet connection and you can complete onboarding, but this could cause hiccups and challenges during the installation period. If you need to contact support, be aware that it will be harder for us to remotely troubleshoot with a slow network connection.

data.name: Help_Scale_Q1_Answer2
data.value: Ensure all cables are intact and undamaged. Any cut cables will need to be replaced by a scale technician before CattleSorting can operate.

data.name: Help_Scale_Q1_Answer3
data.value: Ensure the scale cable is securely connected to the tech box.

data.name: Help_Scale_Q1_Answer5
data.value: The scale head may need to be configured. See next question.

data.name: Help_Scale_Q2
data.value: Do certain scale heads need to be configured?

data.name: Help_Scale_Q2_Answer1
data.value: Yes, Avery Weigh-Tronix scale heads need to be manually configured by the scale tech before weight data can be sent to CattleSorting. There could be other scale heads that need manually configured, too.

data.name: Help_Scale_Q3
data.value: What do I do if the rate is under 2 Hz?

data.name: Help_Scale_Q3_Answer1
data.value: Call a scale tech to adjust this setting. CattleSorting can receive weights when rate is between 1-1.9 Hz although this is not ideal. CattleSorting cannot use weights for sort decision if under 1.0 Hz.

data.name: Help_Scale_Q4_Answer1
data.value: Only rate is relevant to check. The other information is helpful for the scale tech to know, but it is not something that install team needs to check.

data.name: Help_UHFEID_Q1_Answer1
data.value: The UHF should show connected. If not, follow the same diagnostics for ethernet network, except the equipment it is plugged into a "SharkTap" network splitter that may be located either in a protected box or in an enclosed room near the processing chute.

data.name: Help_UHFEID_Q1_Answer2
data.value: The SharkTap power light. Fix the power if not lit up.

data.name: Help_UHFEID_Q1_Answer3
data.value: All three Ethernet ports on the SharkTap should show a solid light and possibly also blinking lights.

data.name: Help_UHFEID_Q1_Answer4
data.value: See if any other equipment is also receiving UHF data. If not, there may be a problem with the UHF reader or its configuration and you should contact the provider of the UHF reader.

data.name: Help_UHFEID_Q1_Answer5
data.value: Check or replace cables. The two ports on opposite sides go to whatever equipment is reading and controlling the UHF reader, and the other goes to the UHF reader. The bottom/middle port goes to the CattleSorting system.
